adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/larkcalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the refresh flow now conditionally routes through `refreshOAuthTokens(...)`. When `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT && credential.userId` are set, `refreshOAuthTokens` calls `process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` (a Cal.com-defined sync endpoint) instead of Lark’s `/authen/v1/refresh_access_token`. The code then still passes that response into `handleLarkError<RefreshTokenResp>(resp, ...)`, which is Lark-specific and (by intent/name and previous usage) is designed to parse/validate Lark API responses. Nothing in the diff adapts parsing for the sync endpoint’s (potentially different) response shape, so enabling credential sync can plausibly break Lark token refresh at runtime. The finding’s additional claim about a “sibling path deletes the credential outright” is not shown in this diff, but the core mismatch between generic sync response and Lark-specific handler is diff-grounded.
